item.title: Cocklebiddy Cave - 6N48
item.description:
From ASF

About

Cocklebiddy Cave is over 6.5km long and is the longest single underwater passage in Australia. The entrance is in a degraded doline 120m long and a steep talus slope beneath overhang at the North end leads to large chamber 360 x 45 x 30m high with 180m long lake. The lake contains “mud islands”.

It is possible to snorkel the lake to look down at the first sump, the water can be muddy after rain.

item.title: Madura Cave
item.description:
From CaveDB

access track is first left off road from madura road house

small enterence hole to left hand side of depression. large cave with solution tube hole to surface mid way into first chamber.

cave splits into two tunnels with soft sediment on floor getting smaller as you go through. tunnels go for a few hundred meters

ASF has a cave tracker in the left hand side of the tunnel around 150m into cave.

item.title: Murra-El-Elevyn - 6N47
item.description:
Other Descriptions

About

Also known as Cocklebiddy 3 Mile Cave, the entrance is a small overhanging doline 20m in diameter. A 20m pitch leads to a loose talus and silt slope which becomes a boulder floored passage after the doline. The passage continues to a small lake at 89m. There are wetas near the entrance of the cave. There was a thylacine carcase found on early trips to the cave.

item.title: Tommy Graham's Cave - 6N56
item.description:
Other Descriptions

About

The entrance to the cave is a large doline 50m in diameter. The obvious route into the doline leads to short cave below the Northwest cliff line.

The main cave has been described as a “wombat- sized hole” which is found in the Southeast end of the doline, about 3m down from the level of the plain. There is a visitor book on a rock shelf in the entrance. The way on is not obvious and goes through a rock squeeze at the end of the low entrance chamber.

item.title: Weebubbie Cave - 6N2
item.description:
From CaveDB

Depth: 40+ metres (130+’) Visibility: 30+ metres (100+’) Water temperature: 17-19°C (63-66°F)

Other Descriptions

About

Description: The entrance to Weebubbie Cave is a large doline 45m in diameter, with a boulder “saddle” at its base. A large main passage with a broken rock floor leads to two lakes at 84m below the surface. The route through the cave is track marked with reflective markers. The cave contains bats and bacterial colonies.
